2. The brief facts of the Plaintiff's case is as under-
The 1st plaintiff is the absolute owner of the land measuring 29 guntas or 31,581 sq. ft.
Situated in Sy. No.2/1 of Vijinapura Village, at present situated within the limits of CMC K.R.Puram, Bangalore, fully described in the schedule-A hereto.
The plaintiffs 2 to 8 and the 2nd defendant are the purchasers of the sites in the layout formed in schedule-A property.
The plaintiffs 2 to 8 are the owners of the sites described in the schedule-B to H hereto, to whom the 1st plaintiff has sold the said sites described in schedule-B to H.

The 2 nd defendant is the purchaser of one of the sites in the layout formed in the schedule-A property to whom the 1st plaintiff has sold the site described in schedule-I described in schedules-B to I are referred to as schedule-B property, schedule-C property.

Schedule-A property purchased by the 1st plaintiff measuring about 31,581 sq. ft. from Smt.Fathima Bi and others by a sale deed dated 29.09.2004 registered as Document No.KRI-I-18150/2004-05 Book-I, stored in CD.No.KRID 74 on 29.09.2004.
1st plaintiff formed a layout dividing schedule-A property into sites providing approach roads in the layout so formed.
He had sold the sites described in the schedules-B to H to the plaintiffs No.2 to 8.
The 3 rd plaintiff Sri.S.Ibrahim has put up a residential building comprising Ground, First and Second Floors in schedule-C property and he is residing in the said building.

The plaintiffs 2 to 8 protested against the trespass committed by the 1st defendant.

The fact remains that no portion of 29 guntas of land described in the schedule-A has been acquired and no compensation was paid passing an award in accordance with the provisions of Land Acquisition Act.
As is evident from the sale deeds produced in respect of sites described in schedules A to H & I, the plaintiffs 1 to 8 and the 2nd defendant had invested heavily on the said properties.
The 1st plaintiff, who sold the said sites described in the schedules B to I, has invested heavily to form the layout by dividing the land into sites by providing approach roads.

The 1st defendant all of a sudden without notice to the plaintiffs and the 2 nd defendant and without paying property taxes to the CMC KR Puram, in respect of the properties described in the schedules hereto started interfering with peaceful possession and enjoyment of the schedule properties by the plaintiffs.
After putting construction, having allowed the 3rd plaintiff to put up construction in 'C' schedule property, the 1st defendant tried to demolish the construction.

To protect his rights, title and interest, the 3rd plaintiff filed a suit in O.S.No.4325/2006, on the file of Ramesh B N vs Multi Disciplinary Training Centre on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119333350/

The 1st defendant again started continuing the digging trenches for putting up compound wall on 22.06.2007.

The plaintiffs will be put to irreparable loss and injury if the 1st defendant is not restrained from trespassing and digging the schedule properties for the purpose of putting up compound wall without any authority whatsoever.
The plaintiffs who are bonafide purchasers for valid consideration, will be put to irreparable loss and injury if their peaceful possession of the schedule properties is not protected.
The 1st defendant having influence and money power has brought the police to the schedule properties to put up compound wall, which has not been put up so far by the 1st defendant.

Plaintiffs having invested huge sums of money over the properties will be put to irreparable loss and injury, if the 1st defendant is not restrained from illegally interfering with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the schedule properties by the plaintiffs.
Hence, the plaintiffs filed this suit.

In order to maintain the suit for bare injunction and to get the equitable remedy.
The plaintiff must be in law possession as on the date of initiating the suit.
In the instant case the plaintiffs are not in a physical possession and enjoyment of any portion of the survey No.2/1 as described in schedule in plaint.

It is stated that, the land bearing Sy.No.2/1 situated at Vijinapur measuring 0.06 guntas had been acquired by the Government of Karnataka vide Gazette Notification No.LAQ (1) CR 59/78-79 dated 16th October 1979 and RD 143 ACQ 80 dated 30th October 1980 and was handed over to this 1st defendant organization.

The Government of Karnataka has acquired the land measuring 16A.37G vide Gazzette Notification dated 4th March 1954 and registered the sale deed in favour of KVIC on 19.10.1984 and handed over to this organization.

The defendant herein filed the comprehensive suit for declaration of title against the vendor of plaintiff in O.S.No.8062/2008 and plaintiff No.3 filed O.S.No.4325/2006 before this Court.
Both the suits O.S.No.8062/2008 and O.S.No.4325/2006 are clubbed by this Court and witness examined in O.S.No.8062/2008.

On that suit by considering the title deeds of the vendor of plaintiff herein this Court is of the opinion that the suit schedule properties herein which is also suit schedule property in O.S.No.8062/2009 belongs to vendor of plaintiff herein and declared the vendor of the plaintiff as the absolute owner of the suit schedule property.
I am of the opinion that before proceedings to discuss about the rival contentions raised by the parties it is correct to mention about the admitted facts.

When such observation made by this Court that declaring the vendor of the plaintiff herein as the absolute owner of the suit schedule property and also the consequential relief of permanent injunction is decreed in favour of the vendor of plaintiff herein.
However, when this Court is of the opinion that the vendor of the plaintiff herein Smt.Fathimabi acquired title over the suit schedule property on the strength of the order passed by Land Tribunal.
When such being the case the defendant even in this case also not produced the final notification regarding acquisition of suit schedule property by its Department.
Besides, the defendant also not produced in respect of any compensation received by the original owner of the suit schedule property.

Hence, once the title is declared by this Court along with consequential reliefs in favour of vendor of plaintiff herein the document i.e. Ex.P-1 absolute Sale Deed produced by the plaintiff herein is valid sale by its vendor as per the observation of this court the vendor of the plaintiff has got absolute right over the suit schedule property.
Hence, in view of the above discussions the plaintiff proves issue No.1 & 2.
Accordingly, I answer these Issues in Affirmative.
14. ISSUE NO.3:
In view of my findings on the above Issues, I proceed to pass the following - ORDER

The suit of the Plaintiffs is hereby DECREED with cost The 1st defendant, their agents,
servants, or anybody claiming through them are permanently restrained from interfering with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule properties by the plaintiffs.
Draw decree accordingly.

 III ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND  SESSIONS JUDGE, BENGALURU  JUDGMENT This present suit is filed by the plaintiff against the 1 st defendant a) permanently restraining the 1st defendant, their agents and servants or any body else claiming through them from interfering with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the properties described in Schedules-A to H by the plaintiffs and altering the relevant records in their favour, without due process of law by granting permanent injunction.
b) granting costs of the suit to the plaintiffs to be paid by the 1st defendant.
opennyai_summary.facts:
The plaintiffs 2 to 8 protested against the trespass committed by the 1st defendant.
The 1st plaintiff, who sold the said sites described in the schedules B to I, has invested heavily to form the layout by dividing the land into sites by providing approach roads.
The 1st defendant all of a sudden without notice to the plaintiffs and the 2 nd defendant and without paying property taxes to the CMC KR Puram, in respect of the properties described in the schedules hereto started interfering with peaceful possession and enjoyment of the schedule properties by the plaintiffs.
After putting construction, having allowed the 3rd plaintiff to put up construction in 'C' schedule property, the 1st defendant tried to demolish the construction.
The plaintiffs will be put to irreparable loss and injury if the 1st defendant is not restrained from trespassing and digging the schedule properties for the purpose of putting up compound wall without any authority whatsoever.
The plaintiffs who are bonafide purchasers for valid consideration, will be put to irreparable loss and injury if their peaceful possession of the schedule properties is not protected.
The defendant center has taken legal steps to protect its interest including the property which the 3rd plaintiff is involved in O.S.No.4325/2006.
The 1st defendant having absolute rights, interest has put up compound wall.
The suit as brought out by the plaintiff is not maintainable in law as such the suit is liable to be dismissed.
In order to maintain the suit for bare injunction and to get the equitable remedy.
The plaintiff must be in law possession as on the date of initiating the suit.
opennyai_summary.issue:
4. On the above rival contentions my predecessor in the office framed the following issues :-
ISSUES 1.
Whether the plaintiff prove that they were in lawful possession and enjoyment of the schedule property as on the date of suit?
2. Whether the plaintiffs prove the alleged interference?
3. What Order or Decree?
5.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The plaintiffs filed this suit for the relief of permanent injunction claiming that they are the absolute owners in possession and enjoyment of the schedule properties.
The plaintiffs who are bonafide purchasers for valid consideration.
The defendant who has no manner of right, title, interest over the schedule property illegally interfering with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the schedule properties by the plaintiffs.
Hence, the plaintiffs filed this suit.
The Government of Karnataka has acquired the land measuring 16A.37G vide Gazzette Notification dated 4th March 1954 and registered the sale deed in favour of KVIC on 19.10.1984 and handed over to this organization.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the suit.
The defendant herein filed the comprehensive suit for declaration of title against the vendor of plaintiff in O.S.No.8062/2008 and plaintiff No.3 filed O.S.No.4325/2006 before this Court.
On that suit by considering the title deeds of the vendor of plaintiff herein this Court is of the opinion that the suit schedule properties herein which is also suit schedule property in O.S.No.8062/2009 belongs to vendor of plaintiff herein and declared the vendor of the plaintiff as the absolute owner of the suit schedule property.
Hence, once the title is declared by this Court along with consequential reliefs in favour of vendor of plaintiff herein the document i.e. Ex.P-1 absolute Sale Deed produced by the plaintiff herein is valid sale by its vendor as per the observation of this court the vendor of the plaintiff has got absolute right over the suit schedule property.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly, I answer these Issues in Affirmative.
In view of my findings on the above Issues, I proceed to pass the following - ORDER
The suit of the Plaintiffs is hereby DECREED with cost The 1st defendant, their agents,
servants, or anybody claiming through them are permanently restrained from interfering with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule properties by the plaintiffs.
Draw decree accordingly.
